newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't switches drafter of re-election law.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't switches drafter of re-election law.

text.p: Parties allied to the Brazilian government have agreed to change the deputy appointed to draw up a bill allowing presidential re-election, officials said.

A spokeswoman for the government's chief whip in the lower house, Benito Gama, said Deputy Jose Murcio Monteiro had decided to leave the drafting of the constitutional amendment to fellow Liberal Front Party (PFL) deputy, Vic Pires Franco.

Opposition parties had vowed to challenge Monteiro's appointment because he had co-authored the original proposal for a constitutional amendment on re-election, and could not therefore, according to house rules, draw up the new version.
"Deputy Murcio decided it would be best to desist to avoid any challenge in the STF (Supreme Federal Tribunal) and to clear up this confusion," the spokeswoman said.
The new lawmaking advocate for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's re-election bid is a new deputy but one held in esteem by Cardoso, she said.
The government hopes to present the re-election bill for a vote in a special committee by early January.
